summary_html:
中国部分要点

  • 中国这一行有三股力量：国企及其研究院（中石化、国家电网、宝武、有研等）贡献了大部分企业论文；国家资本（国家创投引导基金、兵器装备集团、地方国资）在量子计算融资中唱主角；新一代创业公司（晶泰、深势、英矽、剂泰、本源、量旋、玻色）在 2024–2026 年集中上市或冲刺 IPO。
  • 2026 年是中国量子融资的爆发年：一季度融资 32.0 亿元，超过 2025 全年；本源量子估值一年内从 69 亿元涨到 210 亿元，国仪量子 8 月科创板上市首日市值约 450 亿元。
  • AI 药物发现同样放量：2026 年前 9 个月融资 157.7 亿元，超过前三年之和；晶泰科技 2025 年收入增长 201% 并首次盈利，但约 45% 来自一笔授权交易。
  • 中国缺的是北美那种独立的计算化学软件公司：没有中国的 Schrödinger，Gaussian、VASP 等国外软件仍是主力，深势科技和鸿之微是少数国产替代。
summary_html_en:
Key points for China

  • Three forces shape the field in China: state-owned enterprises and their institutes (Sinopec, State Grid, Baowu, GRINM and others) write most corporate papers; state capital (the national venture guidance fund, China South Industries Group, local government funds) leads quantum computing rounds; and a new generation of start-ups (XtalPi, DP Technology, Insilico, METiS, Origin Quantum, SpinQ, QBoson) listed or headed for IPOs in 2024–2026.
  • 2026 is the breakout year for Chinese quantum funding: Q1 alone raised RMB 3.20B, more than all of 2025; Origin Quantum's valuation rose from RMB 6.9B to RMB 21B in a year, and CIQTEK listed on the STAR Market in August at about RMB 45B on day one.
  • AI drug discovery is surging too: RMB 15.77B raised in the first nine months of 2026, more than the previous three years combined; XtalPi grew revenue 201% in 2025 and made its first profit, but about 45% came from one licensing deal.
  • What China lacks is North America's independent computational chemistry software vendors: there is no Chinese Schrödinger, foreign codes such as Gaussian and VASP still dominate, and DP Technology and Hongzhiwei are among the few domestic alternatives.
outlook_html:
中国前瞻：三个判断

  • 量子计算进入「上市窗口」。本源、玻色、图灵已做 IPO 辅导备案，科创板拟把量子列为重点行业。未来两年大概率有 2–3 家上市，估值高度依赖政策与国资定价，收入仍以科研和政府项目为主（本源 2024 年收入不到 1 亿元）。
  • AI 药物发现从「融资故事」转向「授权收入」。晶泰与 DoveTree、华深智药与赛诺菲的交易说明，中国 AI 药企的变现路径是把分子授权给海外药企。风险是收入集中、里程碑兑现率低。
  • 国产计算化学软件是政策缺口。「人工智能+」意见把 AI for Science 列为「十五五」重点；美国实体清单曾让哈工大、哈工程无法使用 MATLAB。若类似限制扩展到化学软件，深势、鸿之微等国产平台会成为直接受益者——这是推断，不是已发生的事实。
outlook_html_en:
Outlook for China: three judgements

  • Quantum computing enters its listing window. Origin Quantum, QBoson and TuringQ have filed for IPO tutoring, and the STAR Market plans to name quantum a priority industry. Two or three listings in the next two years look likely; valuations depend heavily on policy and state pricing, and revenue still comes mostly from research and government projects (Origin earned under RMB 100M in 2024).
  • AI drug discovery moves from funding stories to licensing income. The XtalPi–DoveTree and Helixon–Sanofi deals show that Chinese AI drug companies make money by licensing molecules to overseas pharma. The risks are concentrated revenue and a low rate of milestone payouts.
  • Domestic computational chemistry software is the policy gap. The AI Plus opinions name AI for Science a priority for the 15th Five-Year Plan, and the US Entity List once cut Harbin Institute of Technology and Harbin Engineering University off from MATLAB. If similar limits reach chemistry software, domestic platforms such as DP Technology and Hongzhiwei would benefit directly. That is an inference, not something that has happened.
method_html:
中国部分的方法

中国企业名单由人工整理（51 家），每家的融资、估值和收入都对照了公开报道或财报，并按 A（财报/官方）、B（媒体/数据库）、C（本报告估计）标注。人民币按 1 美元 = 7.2 元、港元按 0.128 美元折算。「数亿元」一类的模糊金额一律按估计（C）处理。论文语料用与北美相同的 OpenAlex 检索，限定作者单位为中国大陆、香港或澳门的企业。员工人数均为量级估计，没有可靠来源。
method_html_en:
Method for the China section

The list of 51 Chinese companies was curated by hand. Each company's funding, valuation and revenue was checked against public reports or filings and labelled A (filings/official), B (media/database) or C (this report's estimate). RMB is converted at 7.2 per US dollar and HK dollars at US$0.128. Vague amounts such as "several hundred million RMB" are always treated as estimates (C). The paper corpus uses the same OpenAlex queries as North America, restricted to company affiliations in mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau. Employee counts are order-of-magnitude estimates with no reliable source.
compare_html: 两边最大的差别在「谁在付钱」。北美的钱主要来自风险资本和上市公司的软件收入；中国的钱越来越多来自国家引导基金和国资，并在 2026 年出现上市潮。北美有成熟的独立软件商，中国则是国企研究院撑起论文量、创业公司撑起估值。
compare_html_en: The biggest difference is who pays. In North America the money comes mostly from venture capital and listed software revenue; in China it increasingly comes from state guidance funds and state investors, with a wave of listings in 2026. North America has mature independent software vendors, while in China state-owned research institutes supply the paper volume and start-ups supply the valuations.
